I’m extremely disappointed with my experience at Bark Club. I used to bring my previous dog here frequently back when this location was Pinky’s, and I always had a good enough experience to feel comfortable bringing my new dog here. Unfortunately, I will not be coming back after this.

My dog is a Cocker Spaniel, and I specifically asked for a Cocker Spaniel cut. What I got was nowhere near what I expected. They shaved the top of his head and basically his entire body extremely short, while leaving longer hair hanging from the bottom with barely any blending or fading. He essentially looks bald on top with random longer hair underneath. I’m including before and after pictures because the difference is honestly insane. A haircut does NOT mean shaving a dog practically down to the skin, especially when that is not what I asked for.

What bothered me even more was that they made me pay BEFORE I was even allowed to see my dog or the haircut I was paying for. The interaction at checkout also felt rushed and rude.

I didn’t complain when I first saw him because at that point I thought, whatever, hair grows back. But then, as soon as we were leaving the parking lot, my dog threw up in my car. I found out that he had been fed something while he was there, even though I never gave permission for anyone to feed him anything. I had to pull over and clean my car, and after getting home, he continued throwing up. I have no idea what he was given or why he was given food without asking me first, but the fact that he became sick immediately afterward is extremely concerning.

Between a haircut that looked nothing like what I requested, being charged $75 before I could even see the result, the customer service, and my dog being fed something without my permission and then repeatedly vomiting afterward, I am completely dissatisfied with this experience.

I trusted this location because of my previous experiences when it was Pinky’s, but unfortunately, I cannot recommend Bark Club and will not be bringing my dog back.

I've been taking my dog Verónica to Bark Club for over five years. Throughout this time, I’ve been a loyal and consistent customer, trusting that my pet would be in good hands. However, every time I have to deal with the woman at the front desk, the experience turns unpleasant, frustrating, and downright disrespectful.

Today was the last straw. This woman, whose attitude is far from professional, once again insisted—like she has before—that Verónica was “full of knots” and that the only solution was to completely shave her down. That is simply not true. I take great care of my dog’s coat: I brush her regularly, keep her clean, and never let her get neglected. Yet this person, without even giving Verónica a proper look or showing the slightest willingness to listen, makes hasty decisions that clearly prioritize staff convenience over the animal’s well-being.

This isn’t the first time it has happened. But today I left feeling disrespected and deeply disappointed, as if I didn’t know how to care for my own pet. I walked out upset and convinced that as long as this woman remains the face of the business, Bark Club does not deserve our trust. Her attitude is rude, indifferent, and most concerning of all—she shows zero empathy and no sense of professionalism.

My suggestion to management is simple: if you truly care about retaining your clients and maintaining a respectable reputation, you should seriously consider replacing this receptionist with someone who genuinely loves animals, knows how to treat people, and is willing to offer proper, respectful service. A pet business needs people with passion and dedication—not someone who clearly just wants to clock in and push customers out the door.

It’s a shame that one single person can ruin the entire experience at a place I once considered trustworthy. For now, I won’t be coming back.
